scrambled_eggs.name: Classic French Soft-Curd Scrambled Eggs
scrambled_eggs.description: Velvety, slow-cooked scrambled eggs with butter and chives.

substitutions.butter: Ghee or olive oil (1.5 tablespoons), but cold butter provides the creamiest emulsion.
substitutions.heavy cream: 1 tablespoon of whole milk, 1 tablespoon of creme fraiche, or 1 tablespoon of sour cream.
substitutions.chives: Finely minced scallion greens or fresh flat-leaf parsley.

steps.instruction: Crack four eggs into a cold, unheated nonstick skillet and add two tablespoons of cubed cold butter.
Place the pan over medium-low heat and continuously stir with a silicone spatula for two minutes until curds start forming.
Pull the skillet off the heat for thirty seconds while continuing to stir to prevent overcooking.
Return to low heat for sixty seconds until velvety curds set, then fold in one tablespoon of heavy cream, salt, and chives.
Transfer immediately to a warm plate and serve soft and custardy.

cacio_e_pepe.name: Authentic Roman Cacio e Pepe
cacio_e_pepe.description: Minimalist pasta with freshly cracked black peppercorns and creamy Pecorino Romano emulsion.

ingredients.name: pecorino romano
ingredients.unit: grams, very finely grated on microplane

ingredients.name: pasta water
ingredients.unit: cup, starchy water reserved from boiling

substitutions.pecorino romano: A 50/50 blend of Parmigiano Reggiano and Pecorino, or pure aged Parmesan if Pecorino is unavailable.
substitutions.black peppercorns: Coarse freshly cracked black pepper, but toasting whole peppercorns gives the best flavor.

steps.instruction: Bring four cups of lightly salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti for eight minutes until very al dente.
Toast cracked black pepper in a wide dry skillet over medium heat for one minute until fragrant.
Ladle half a cup of hot starchy pasta water into the pepper skillet to create a simmering pepper broth.
In a small bowl, whisk grated pecorino with a splash of warm pasta water until it forms a smooth paste.
Transfer cooked pasta into the skillet, remove from heat completely, and vigorously toss with the pecorino cream for ninety seconds until silky.

ribeye_steak.name: Reverse-Sear Thick-Cut Ribeye with Garlic-Herb Butter
ribeye_steak.description: A thick-cut ribeye salted, gently brought to temperature, and hard-seared with foaming herb butter.

substitutions.ribeye steak: Thick-cut New York strip or bone-in porterhouse (at least 1.5 inches thick).
substitutions.unsalted butter: Ghee or cultured salted butter (reduce kosher salt slightly).

steps.instruction: Season the ribeye thoroughly on all sides with kosher salt and let it dry brine uncovered in the fridge for at least two hours.
Bake on a wire rack at 225 degrees Fahrenheit for thirty minutes until internal temperature hits 115 degrees for medium rare.
Heat a heavy cast iron skillet over high heat with one tablespoon of oil until smoking hot for three minutes.
Sear the ribeye for one minute per side to develop a deep brown crust.
Drop the heat, add butter, crushed garlic, and herbs, and spoon the foaming butter over the steak for two minutes.
Rest the steak on a warm cutting board for ten minutes before carving.

chocolate_chip_cookies.name: Brown Butter Sea Salt Chocolate Chip Cookies
chocolate_chip_cookies.description: Chewy center, crispy edges, nutty browned butter, and melted dark chocolate pools.

substitutions.dark brown sugar: Light brown sugar with a teaspoon of molasses, or coconut sugar.
substitutions.dark chocolate chunks: Semi-sweet chocolate chips or chopped milk chocolate.
substitutions.all-purpose flour: 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend with xanthan gum.

steps.instruction: Melt two sticks of butter in a saucepan over medium heat for five minutes until foamy, nutty, and golden brown.
Whisk cooled browned butter with brown sugar and granulated sugar for two minutes until smooth and glossy.
Beat in the whole egg, extra yolk, and vanilla extract until the mixture turns pale and ribbony.
Fold in flour and baking soda with a spatula until just combined, then gently fold in chocolate chunks.
Bake scooped dough balls at 375 degrees Fahrenheit for ten minutes until edges are golden and centers soft.
Sprinkle immediately with flaky sea salt and cool on the pan for five minutes before transferring.

chicken_tikka_masala.name: Creamy Spiced Chicken Tikka Masala
chicken_tikka_masala.description: Tender marinated chicken pieces simmered in an aromatic, velvety spiced tomato-cream curry sauce.

substitutions.heavy cream: Full-fat coconut milk or soaked blended cashew paste for a rich dairy-free sauce.
substitutions.chicken thighs: Paneer cubes, extra-firm pressed tofu, or boneless chicken breast.
substitutions.plain yogurt: Greek yogurt thinned with a tablespoon of lemon juice.

steps.instruction: Toss chicken with yogurt, garlic-ginger paste, garam masala, and salt, then marinate for at least twenty minutes.
Sear marinated chicken in a smoking hot skillet or under high broiler for seven minutes until charred in spots.
In a deep pan, saute onions, cumin, coriander, and remaining ginger-garlic in two tablespoons of butter for five minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and simmer on low heat for ten minutes until the sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in heavy cream and cooked chicken pieces, simmering together for five minutes until rich and fragrant.

fluffy_buttermilk_pancakes.name: Golden Diner-Style Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
fluffy_buttermilk_pancakes.description: Thick, cloud-soft pancakes with crispy golden edges and warm melted butter.

substitutions.buttermilk: 2 cups whole milk mixed with 2 tablespoons lemon juice or white vinegar, rested for 5 minutes.
substitutions.all-purpose flour: Whole wheat pastry flour or 1:1 gluten-free flour blend.
substitutions.melted butter: Coconut oil or neutral avocado oil.

steps.instruction: Whisk dry ingredients together in a large bowl, then whisk buttermilk, eggs, and melted butter in a separate jug.
Pour wet ingredients into dry and fold gently until just combined; leave small flour lumps and rest batter for ten minutes.
Heat a cast iron griddle or nonstick pan over medium heat with a light sheen of butter for three minutes.
Pour one third cup of batter per pancake and cook for three minutes until bubbles burst on top and edges look dry.
Flip gently and cook the second side for ninety seconds until puffed and golden brown.

tuscan_garlic_salmon.name: Crispy Tuscan Salmon in Garlic Spinach Cream
tuscan_garlic_salmon.description: Crispy pan-seared salmon fillets bathed in sun-dried tomato and baby spinach cream sauce.

ingredients.name: salmon fillets
ingredients.unit: fillets (approx 180g each), skin-on and patted dry

substitutions.salmon fillets: Trout fillets, sea bass, or thick boneless chicken breast cutlets.
substitutions.heavy cream: Half-and-half thickened with a teaspoon of cornstarch, or culinary coconut cream.
substitutions.baby spinach: Baby kale, Swiss chard leaves, or arugula.

steps.instruction: Season salmon fillets with salt and pepper, then sear skin-side down in a hot skillet with olive oil for five minutes until skin is crackling.
Flip fillets and sear the flesh side for two minutes, then remove to a side plate.
In the same pan, saute sliced garlic and sun-dried tomatoes in two tablespoons of butter for one minute until fragrant.
Pour in heavy cream and parmesan, bring to a gentle simmer for two minutes until velvety and slightly reduced.
Fold in baby spinach until wilted, nestle salmon back into the sauce, and spoon warm cream over the fish for sixty seconds.

guacamole_street_tacos.name: Citrus Carne Asada Tacos with Fresh Guacamole
guacamole_street_tacos.description: Charred marinated flank steak on warm corn tortillas topped with fresh crushed guacamole and cilantro.

substitutions.flank steak: Boneless chicken thighs, portobello mushroom caps, or spiced black beans.
substitutions.corn tortillas: Flour street tortillas or crisp lettuce wraps.
substitutions.fresh limes: Unsweetened bottled lime juice with a splash of orange juice.

steps.instruction: Marinate steak with lime juice, minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, and olive oil for fifteen minutes.
Grill or sear steak in a smoking cast iron skillet for four minutes per side until charred and medium.
Rest steak on a cutting board for eight minutes, then slice thinly against the grain into small ribbons.
Roughly mash avocados with lime juice, salt, diced onion, and cilantro until chunky.
Warm corn tortillas on dry skillet for thirty seconds each, fill with steak ribbons, and crown with guacamole.
